noeuds.schema: Input: Teams, in order (tags separated by a comma)
noeuds.role: Passes the game to the next team. Write the teams in order using their tags (e.g. player,enemy). The first call (for example after "At start") begins with the first team; when every team has played, the turn number goes up. At the start of each turn the local event "tour_<team>" runs if it exists (e.g. "tour_enemy").
noeuds.exemple: put "Go to the next turn" on the "End turn" button.

noeuds.nom: If it is the turn of…
noeuds.role: True if it is the turn of the team written (its tag), False otherwise.
noeuds.exemple: let the player touch their units only during their own turn.

noeuds.role: Remembers that the unit (object A) has played this turn. Everything is cleared when the next turn starts.
noeuds.exemple: stop a hero from moving twice in the same turn.

noeuds.nom: If the unit has already played
noeuds.role: True if the unit (object A) has already played this turn, False otherwise.
noeuds.exemple: refuse to move a hero that has already played.

noeuds.schema: Inputs: Object, Zone type, Number of steps (or range), Color of the cells, Cell visibility (0 = invisible, 100 = solid), Frame around each cell, Write the step count on each cell, Walls block (movement), These tags block the way (separated by commas), Terrain costing more steps (tag=cost, e.g. forest=2, water=3), Zone name (optional: to show several), Range shape (attack and jump), Minimum range (0 = none; 2 = not the first cells), My positions (column,row; e.g. 2,1 ; -2,1 ; 0,3), Remove the cell the object stands on
noeuds.role: Colors the cells the chosen object can move to (or attack). Walls block, and you can add tags that block (other units) and terrains that cost more steps (forest=2). Color, visibility, frame and numbers are adjustable. "Zone name" lets you show several at once (movement in blue, attack in red).
noeuds.exemple: show a hero's movement zone when it is touched.

noeuds.role: Clears the colored cells (all of them, or one named zone).
noeuds.exemple: hide the zone once the hero has arrived.

noeuds.schema: Inputs: Column, Row, Zone name (optional)  →  Outputs: True / False
noeuds.role: True if the cell (column, row) is one of the shown cells. By default: the cell the finger touches. False otherwise.
noeuds.exemple: refuse a move that is too far with "too far!".

noeuds.schema: Inputs: Object, Health points, Attack, Defense, Movement (steps), Attack range (cells), Other statistics (e.g. munitions = 3, armure = 2)
noeuds.role: Gives the object its sheet: health, attack, defense, movement and range (object variables "vie", "attaque", "defense", "mouvement", "portee"). They can be read anywhere with a formula, e.g. =hero.mouvement for the number of steps of the reachable cells. Put this node "At start" of each unit, or in a reusable unit prefab.
noeuds.exemple: create an archer: health 8, attack 4, defense 0, movement 4, range 3.

noeuds.schema: Inputs: Object A, Object B, Attack power (%), Count the defense of the target's terrain, Always at least 1 damage, Destroy the target when its health runs out, Free damage formula (e.g. attacker.attaque * 2 - target.armure); empty = normal calculation  →  Outputs: Still alive / Out of health
noeuds.role: Object A attacks object B: damage = A's attack × power − B's defense − the defense of B's terrain. Two outputs: "Still alive" and "Out of health" (the target is destroyed if the box is ticked). Both objects need a unit sheet.
noeuds.exemple: a hero hits the touched monster.

noeuds.role: Gives health points to the chosen object (object variable "vie", and "vie_max" for the maximum). Read it anywhere with a formula, e.g. =monster.vie, to write it in a text or a bar.
noeuds.exemple: give a monster 10 health points at the start.

noeuds.schema: Inputs: Object, Damage, Destroy the object when its health runs out, Subtract the defense of the terrain it stands on  →  Outputs: Still alive / Out of health
noeuds.role: Removes health points from the object (never below 0). Two outputs: "Still alive" and "Out of health" (the object is destroyed if the box is ticked; "the involved object" stays the one hit).
noeuds.exemple: a hero hits a monster: 3 damage, then a small message depending on the result.

noeuds.role: Gives health points back to the object, without going over its maximum.
noeuds.exemple: a potion that restores 5 health points to the hero.

noeuds.schema: Inputs: Object, Tags of possible targets (comma-separated), Which target to pick?, Range in cells (0 = unlimited; e.g. =monster.portee), Minimum range (0 = none), Range shape, My positions (column,row; e.g. 2,1 ; -2,1), Statistic (for the “statistic” rules, e.g. defense)  →  Outputs: Target found / No target
noeuds.role: Object A looks among the objects that carry one of the requested tags for those WITHIN ITS RANGE (same shapes as “Show reachable cells”), then picks one: the closest, the one with the least or the most health, or the lowest / highest value of a statistic. “Target found” output: it becomes “the involved object” (for Attack, Go to…). “No target” output: nobody in range. Perfect for the intelligence of a monster or a turret.
noeuds.exemple: a monster: “Choose a target” (tag “hero”, the closest, range =monster.range), then “Attack” on “Target found”.

noeuds.schema: Inputs: Object, Columns, Rows, Model objects (names separated by commas)
noeuds.role: Splits object A (the board) into columns and rows and puts in each cell a copy of a model object picked at random (at least 3 models, names separated by commas). There is never a match at the start, and the pieces drop in from the top. Use it before “Play on the grid (match 3)”.
noeuds.exemple: at the start, an 8 x 8 grid of candies "red, orange, yellow, green, blue, pink".

noeuds.schema: Inputs: Object, Finger X position, Finger Y position  →  Outputs: For each matched piece / Move finished / Swap refused
noeuds.role: The heart of a match-3 game (Candy Crush style), to put under “Finger held down”. Touching a piece selects it, touching its neighbour (or sliding the finger to it) swaps them. The swap only stays if it lines up 3 or more identical pieces; otherwise they go back (“Swap refused”). Each matched piece starts “For each matched piece” (the involved object is the piece), then disappears; pieces fall, new ones arrive and combos happen by themselves. When everything is still: “Move finished”. With no possible move, the grid shuffles itself.
noeuds.exemple: “For each matched piece”: +10 points and sparkles on the piece; “Move finished”: one move less.

noeuds.role: Moves all the pieces of object A's grid to new places, without creating a match and keeping at least one possible move.
noeuds.exemple: a "Shuffle" button when the player is stuck.

noeuds.role: Randomly swaps the places of all objects with the chosen tag (Object A = "# tag"). Their child objects follow them.
noeuds.exemple: shuffle the cards of a memory game at the start, or the cups of a shell game.
